reviews.text: Horrible! I took my two dogs in for their summer haircuts and they charged me €90. The problem isn't the price, it's the terrible service. They gave the little one a shapeless cut, and the white coat showed the scissor cuts all over the place. They were there for almost four hours. I don't recommend them at all; they're awful.
We took Nala to get a bath and a nail trim. The service was very pleasant, and Nala came out very clean, soft...like new.

I absolutely do not recommend this place, unless you enjoy being lectured and judged. Two and a half hours per dog for nothing, not even a head wash or ear trim, and... €50. A real shame, honestly. My intention was to be a customer.

Today I took my cat to BenKurt. She's a Persian cat with lots of fur. They treated us wonderfully! It's hard to find a good professional who gets along well with cats, and I found one at BenKurt. Rosa did a fantastic job! A good wash, drying, and brushing. She removed a few knots my cat had. She used the clippers where needed. Everything was quick but not rushed. No stress. And no sedation. You can tell she knows what she's doing. She let my cat set the pace throughout the whole process, without forcing anything at all! I'm so happy (and my cat was too!), as they gave her a treat and a little ball for her collection! Our little one is ready to shine this Christmas! Thank you so much! ♥️
Very professional, Rosa is very nice, the place is a bit small, but the treatment is very friendly

This hair salon offers a wide variety of products, from food and toys to clothing and accessories. Everything is carefully selected and reasonably priced. The most outstanding feature is the friendly and welcoming service from the owner.

Hi, thanks for your comment, although I think there's a slight misunderstanding: yes, I know perfectly well that I booked an appointment at a dog groomer, not with an ethologist. In fact, that's precisely why I expected the person attending to me to have experience working with dogs, not just using clippers.

I understand that not all dogs are the same, but if after a 10-minute "assessment" the verdict was that my dog ​​wasn't suitable—without even attempting a haircut—I'm surprised that this is called a service. And even more so that they charged me 5 euros for that time. Express assessment? Premium diagnosis?

A dog groomer, in addition to handling scissors, should have a basic understanding of behavior, patience, and know how to adapt to dogs who, surprise, aren't always still or happy to be there. Not all dogs are cuddly toys. That's why there are professionals who, beyond the right of admission, have sound judgment, resources, and a true calling.

And no, I didn't confuse the sign. I just thought a dog groomer would know how to handle dogs. Big mistake on my part. But thanks for the encouragement… although what would really help is a little more professionalism instead of sarcasm.
